title: Short extracts: podcasting, open-mic comedy, a cinema conversion

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two friends, Lucy and Sam, talking about the podcast they make together. Lucy speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I've been listening back to our last few episodes, Sam. Something's gone wrong since we left the studio.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: You mean the sound? I know there's a bit of an echo in my kitchen.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: No, the sound's fine, really. Most of our listeners wear headphones on the bus. They'd never notice.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: What bothers me is that we ramble. In the studio, we were paying by the hour, so every minute counted. Now we just chat until we get bored.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Hmm. I suppose the last one did run to nearly ninety minutes.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Exactly. And our guests have been brilliant lately. It's a shame to bury them in all that waffle.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Fair enough. So what are you proposing? Because I'm not going back to paying studio rent.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Neither am I. But what if we gave ourselves a strict limit? Say, forty-five minutes, with a timer on the table.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: A timer? That sounds a bit like a school exam, to be honest.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Then again, I can't argue with the figures. Our downloads have dropped every single month since the episodes got longer. All right. Let's try it for a month and see.

questions.stem: What does Lucy think is wrong with their recent episodes?

options.A: The recordings contain too much background noise.
options.C: The guests have not been well chosen.

explanation.en: Lucy says 'What bothers me is that we ramble' and 'we just chat until we get bored'. A is the trap: Sam suggests the echo, but Lucy rejects it ('the sound's fine, really'). C is wrong because she calls the guests 'brilliant'.
explanation.cs: Klíčová věta je 'we ramble' (mluvíme bez ladu a skladu, odbíháme od tématu). Past je zvuk: Sam ho zmíní, ale Lucy ho hned odmítne slovy 'No, the sound's fine'. Hosty naopak chválí.

questions.stem: What finally persuades Sam to accept a time limit?

options.A: the cost of hiring a studio
options.B: Lucy's idea of using a timer
options.C: a fall in the number of listeners

explanation.en: Sam says 'I can't argue with the figures. Our downloads have dropped every single month', and only then agrees. A is wrong: he refuses to pay 'studio rent' again. B is wrong: he says the timer sounds 'like a school exam'.
explanation.cs: Sama přesvědčí až čísla: 'Our downloads have dropped' (klesají stažení, tedy posluchači). Studio zmiňuje jen proto, že se do něj vracet nechce, a nápad s časovačem zpočátku zesměšňuje. Pozor na 'Then again' – uvádí obrat v názoru.

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two friends, Nina and Josh, talking about Josh's first performance at a comedy club. Nina speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So how did your first open-mic night go, Josh? Be honest.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, nobody threw anything. The first two minutes were awful, though. I rushed my opening joke, and it fell completely flat.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh no. Did you panic?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Strangely, no. Something happened after that. A man in the front row coughed really loudly, right in the middle of a sentence.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I made a comment about it, and the whole room laughed. After that, I relaxed and just talked to them.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So the best moment wasn't even something you'd written.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That's what's so annoying. I spent three weeks polishing that material. My sister made me practise it in front of her every evening.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Still, all that practice probably gave you the confidence to improvise.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Maybe. But I came away thinking the script matters far less than I'd assumed. Next time, I'll go up with a few ideas on a card and see where the audience takes me.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Isn't that a bit risky?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Probably. But it was the only part of the night I actually enjoyed.

questions.stem: What does Josh say about the start of his performance?

options.A: He delivered his first joke too quickly.
options.B: He forgot the words of his opening joke.
options.C: He was interrupted by a member of the audience.

explanation.en: Josh says 'I rushed my opening joke', so he told it too quickly. B is not said: he told the joke, but 'it fell completely flat'. C is the trap: the man coughed, but Josh says this happened 'after that', not at the start.
explanation.cs: 'Rushed' znamená uspěchat, říct příliš rychle. Kašlající divák je past: Josh výslovně říká 'Something happened after that', tedy až po začátku. 'Fell flat' neznamená zapomenout text, ale že vtip nezabral.

questions.stem: What has Josh concluded from the experience?

options.A: His sister's help was more useful than he realised.
options.B: Careful preparation is what gave him confidence.
options.C: Reacting to the audience matters more than prepared material.

explanation.en: Josh says 'the script matters far less than I'd assumed' and plans to 'see where the audience takes me'. B is Nina's opinion, and Josh answers 'Maybe. But...', which rejects it. A is wrong: he mentions his sister only to show how much he practised.
explanation.cs: Názor B vyslovuje Nina, ne Josh. Jeho 'Maybe. But...' je typický zdvořilý nesouhlas. Sestru zmiňuje jen jako příklad toho, kolik času strávil přípravou, která se nakonec ukázala jako méně důležitá.

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two architects, Helen and Marek, discussing a plan to convert an old cinema. Helen speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Have you seen the latest drawings for the cinema, Marek? The developer's changed the plans again.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I have. They've dropped the rooftop restaurant, which I'm not sorry about. It would have spoiled the skyline.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Agreed. But now they want to remove the original front entrance and put in a glass one.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That's what really worries me. The tiled entrance is the one thing people in this town remember. Their grandparents queued there on Saturday nights.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: The developer says it isn't wide enough for wheelchair users, though.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Which is a genuine problem. But the doorway could be widened at the side without destroying the tiles. I sketched an option last night.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let me guess. You'd like me to present it at Thursday's meeting.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, you're much better at handling him than I am. He actually listens to you.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Flattery won't work on me. Fine. But only if you work out the costs first. He'll ask for them straight away.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Deal. I'll have the figures ready by Wednesday.

questions.stem: What concerns Marek most about the new plans?

options.A: the loss of the rooftop restaurant
options.B: the removal of the original entrance
options.C: the developer's frequent changes to the design

explanation.en: About the glass entrance, Marek says 'That's what really worries me' because people 'remember' the tiled one. A is wrong: he is 'not sorry' the restaurant was dropped. C is mentioned by Helen ('changed the plans again'), but Marek does not complain about it.
explanation.cs: 'That's what really worries me' přímo ukazuje na vchod. U restaurace říká 'I'm not sorry' (nevadí mi to, spíš naopak). Časté změny plánů zmiňuje Helen, ale Marek k nim žádný postoj nevyjadřuje. Přístup pro vozíčkáře uznává jako problém, ale hned nabízí řešení.

options.A: to get her to present his proposal
options.B: to show he shares her view of the restaurant
options.C: to thank her for showing him the drawings

explanation.en: Helen guesses 'You'd like me to present it', and Marek replies 'you're much better at handling him'. Helen sees the purpose at once: 'Flattery won't work on me.' B is wrong: they agreed about the restaurant earlier, without praise. C is wrong: he had already seen the drawings.
explanation.cs: Otázka se ptá na účel (purpose): Marek lichotí, aby Helen návrh prezentovala za něj. Helen to sama pojmenuje: 'Flattery won't work on me' (lichotky na mě neplatí). Výkresy už Marek viděl ('I have'), takže C nedává smysl.
